gloss: to use a metaphor; to liken; to compare figuratively

definitions.gloss: to use a metaphor; to liken; to compare figuratively
definitions.explanation: To express something by comparing it to something else in a figurative way. Often used in literary criticism, rhetoric, and academic writing.

examples.japanese: {人生|じんせい}を{旅|たび}に{比喩|ひゆ}する。
examples.english: To liken life to a journey.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{社会|しゃかい}を{機械|きかい}に{比喩|ひゆ}して{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.english: He explained society by likening it to a machine.

examples.japanese: {時間|じかん}の{流|なが}れを{川|かわ}の{流|なが}れに{比喩|ひゆ}するのは、{古|ふる}くからある{表現|ひょうげん}だ。
examples.english: Comparing the passage of time to the flow of a river is an expression that has existed since ancient times.

notes:
The verb form of the noun {比喩|ひゆ} (metaphor, simile, figure of speech). The pattern is typically AをBに{比喩|ひゆ}する (to liken A to B). More formal and literary than {例|たと}える.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- AをBに{比喩|ひゆ}する: to liken A to B
- {比喩|ひゆ}して{言|い}えば: speaking metaphorically
- {比喩|ひゆ}される: to be compared to (passive)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {例|たと}える: to compare, to liken — more common in everyday speech
- {喩|たと}える: variant kanji of the above, literary
- {なぞらえる}: to compare, to liken — literary, often implies modeling after something

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {比喩|ひゆ}していませんでした
